dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: māyā vimohinī nāma kalāyāḥ kalanaṃ sthitam | ityādidharmaṃ tattvānāṃ kalayan na pṛthag bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 95: Singh records the variant reading kalayan nā pṛthag bhavet ('such a person becomes isolated, i.e. established in the Self').
dharana.rendering: 'Māyā is the one that bewilders; the function of kalā is limiting activity': contemplating in this way the characteristics of the principles (tattvas), one no longer remains separate.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: Abhinavagupta defines māyā as the power that veils the Self and shows diversity; through her coverings (kañcukas) she limits activity, knowledge, desire, time and causation. Knowing their functions, the yogī does not lose sight of the wholeness of reality and sees manifestation as Śiva's expression. Singh records a variant, kalayan nā pṛthag bhavet ('such a person becomes isolated, established in the Self'). Wallis counts this verse as 'not a yukti'.
dharana.technique_name: Seeing Through the Powers That Limit
dharana.instruction: Recognise how time, place, knowledge, ability and desire limit experience, and stop taking those limits as who you are.

source_disagreements: Status as a technique: Singh counts verse 95 as dhāraṇā 72; Wallis marks it 'not a yukti'. Variant kalayan nā pṛthag bhavet recorded by Singh.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 95 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the limiting powers: activity, knowledge, desire, time, causation
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a set of veils (the limiting powers) that, once recognised for what they do, no longer separate one from the whole.
geometry.svg_hint: a few translucent layers in front of a light that shines through them
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Name the veils
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: limits that operate unseen are recognised by name and lose their power to separate. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The functions of the limiting powers, recognised one by one
attention.secondary: Not feeling separate from the whole

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: 'Māyā is the one that bewilders; the function of kalā is limiting activity': contemplating in this way the characteristics of the principles (tattvas), one no longer remains separate.
adiyogi.method_summary: Reflect on how experience is limited: by time, by place, by what one can do, by what one knows, by what one wants. Recognise each as a function, not as who you are. Let the sense of separation from the whole ease.

honesty.disclosure: Door 072 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 72 (verse 95) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 072 is dharana 72, verse 95. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. A reflection, not a test; if it becomes heavy, let it go and rest with the breath. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
